We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied first two templates successfully, got some intermediates. Need to continue applying remaining templates sequentially to generate a route ending in starting materials (maybe simple molecules). We need to construct JSON tree: root molecule is target, then reaction node with template 29646, children are precursors (maybe multiple). Then each precursor may be further broken down with next template etc. The order must be as given, meaning first reaction uses template 29646 to break target into some precursors; then for each precursor we apply next template? Usually a linear route: each step applies next template to one of the precursors, while others are leaf nodes (buyable). We need at least 5 reactions, exactly 5 using those templates.

We need to find applicable precursors for each step. We have applied template 29646 to target, got three possible precursor sets (the result is a tuple of tuples). The result from apply_template gave three possible outcomes: each is a tuple of SMILES strings (maybe two or three). Let's parse result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',))"

So three possible outcomes each with one precursor? Actually each tuple contains one SMILES string. So template 29646 seems to be a protecting group removal? Not sure. But we can choose one outcome to continue.

We need to apply template 1914389 next. We checked matching for first outcome (with Si protecting group) and got True, applied and got two precursors: ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC').

So after second step, we have two precursors. Next template 1914390 should be applied to one of these precursors (maybe the first). We tried matching first precursor and got False. So maybe apply to second precursor? Check matching for second precursor with template 1914390.
